sections.title: Introduction
sections.text:
Welcome. Today we turn to the New Testament and to the event that divides all of history: the birth of Jesus Christ. For centuries, God's people had been waiting. The prophets had promised that one day God would send a Saviour — a King from the family of David. Then, after about four hundred years without a new prophet, an angel appeared.

The story is told in the Gospels of Matthew and Luke. It's a story we often hear at Christmas, but its message is for every day of the year. As you listen, notice who God chose to be part of this story, and what that tells us about the kind of King Jesus is.

sections.title: The Story, Part 1
sections.text:
Seven hundred years earlier, the prophet Isaiah had written these words, in Isaiah chapter seven, verse fourteen: “Therefore the Lord himself shall give you a sign; Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel.”

Now the time had come. God sent the angel Gabriel to a city of Galilee called Nazareth, to a young woman named Mary. Mary was engaged to a man named Joseph, a descendant of King David. Gabriel greeted her, and Mary was troubled, wondering what kind of greeting this was. Luke chapter one, verses thirty and thirty-one: “And the angel said unto her, Fear not, Mary: for thou hast found favour with God. And, behold, thou shalt conceive in thy womb, and bring forth a son, and shalt call his name JESUS.” Gabriel said her son would be great, would be called the Son of the Highest, and would reign forever.

Mary asked how this could be, since she was a virgin. Gabriel explained that the Holy Ghost would come upon her, and the child would be called the Son of God. And he added, “For with God nothing shall be impossible.” Mary's answer is a model of trust: “Behold the handmaid of the Lord; be it unto me according to thy word.”

When Joseph learned that Mary was expecting a child, he was troubled, and he planned to end the engagement quietly. But an angel appeared to him in a dream and said, “Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost.” The angel told him the child's name would be Jesus, “for he shall save his people from their sins.” Matthew explains that this fulfilled Isaiah's prophecy, and that Emmanuel means “God with us.” Joseph obeyed and took Mary as his wife.

sections.title: The Story, Part 2
sections.text:
Then Caesar Augustus ordered a census of the whole Roman world, and everyone had to go to their family's hometown to be registered. So Joseph took Mary, who was expecting her baby, and traveled from Nazareth to Bethlehem, the city of David — just as the prophet Micah had foretold that the ruler of Israel would come from Bethlehem.

While they were there, the time came for the baby to be born. Luke chapter two, verse seven: “And she brought forth her firstborn son, and wrapped him in swaddling clothes, and laid him in a manger; because there was no room for them in the inn.” The King of kings was born in a place where animals were fed.

That same night, shepherds were out in the fields nearby, keeping watch over their flocks. Suddenly an angel of the Lord appeared, the glory of the Lord shone around them, and they were terrified. Luke chapter two, verses ten and eleven: “And the angel said unto them, Fear not: for, behold, I bring you good tidings of great joy, which shall be to all people. For unto you is born this day in the city of David a Saviour, which is Christ the Lord.” Then a multitude of angels appeared, praising God and saying, “Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace, good will toward men.”

The shepherds hurried to Bethlehem and found Mary, Joseph, and the baby lying in a manger, just as the angel said. They told everyone what they had heard, and all who heard it were amazed. But Mary kept all these things and pondered them in her heart.

Some time later, wise men from the east came to Jerusalem, asking, “Where is he that is born King of the Jews? for we have seen his star in the east, and are come to worship him.” King Herod was troubled, and secretly planned to kill the child. The star led the wise men to the house where Jesus was. Matthew chapter two, verse eleven: “they saw the young child with Mary his mother, and fell down, and worshipped him: and when they had opened their treasures, they presented unto him gifts; gold, and frankincense, and myrrh.”

Warned in a dream not to return to Herod, the wise men went home another way. And an angel warned Joseph in a dream to flee to Egypt, and he took the young child and His mother by night and kept them safe there until Herod died.

sections.title: The Lesson
sections.text:
What does the birth of Jesus teach us?

First, God keeps His promises. Hundreds of years before, God promised a virgin birth, a son of David, and a ruler from Bethlehem. Every detail came true. If God kept these promises, we can trust Him to keep His promises to us.

Second, Jesus came for everyone. The first people to hear the news weren't kings or priests — they were ordinary shepherds working the night shift. And then came wise men from a faraway country. From the very beginning, the good news was “to all people.” No one is too ordinary, and no one is too far away.

Third, trusting God sometimes means saying yes before we understand everything. Mary didn't know how God's plan would unfold. Joseph faced embarrassment and hard choices. But both of them said yes to God, and both obeyed.

And finally, Jesus is Emmanuel — God with us. God didn't stay far away from our struggles. He came close, as a baby, and lived among us. That means that whatever you are going through today, you are not alone.

sections.title: Prayer and Reflection
sections.text:
Imagine standing with the shepherds at the manger. What would you want to say to the child who came to save you? Take a moment and say it to Him now.

Let's pray. Lord Jesus, thank You for coming to earth as a baby, to be God with us. Thank You that the good news is for all people, including me. Like Mary, help me say, be it unto me according to Your word. And like the wise men, help me give You my very best. In Your name, Amen.

Thank you for listening. Next time, we'll hear some of the stories Jesus told: His parables.
